elicitation_input.question: where are mucosal associated lymphoid tissues present in the human body and why

llm_generation.text:
Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissues (MALT) are diffuse collections of lymphoid tissue beneath mucosal surfaces, especially in the:

- Gastrointestinal tract, including the intestine, appendix, and stomach (GALT)
- Tonsils and nasopharynx (including Waldeyer’s ring/NALT)
- Respiratory tract and lungs
- Oral cavity and salivary glands
- Thyroid, breast, eyes, and skin

They are present at these sites because mucosal surfaces are major entry points for pathogens and foreign antigens. MALT provides a first line of immune defense by sampling antigens, producing
